correctness.rationale: For compactly supported invariant probability measures of the nominal Newton–Leipnik ODE, invariance gives ∫LF dμ=0 for every polynomial F. Independently differentiated F1=x²/2+z² and F2=(y²+z²)/2 to obtain LF1=−2x²/5+xy+7z²/20 and LF2=−xy−2y²/5+7z²/40. Thus A+B=21C/16 and M=∫xy=2A/5−7C/20. For C>0, t=A/C and M²≤AB give exactly 464t²−637t+49≤0, roots (637±35sqrt257)/928. For C=0 all second moments vanish so μ=δ0. Equality in Cauchy–Schwarz forces y=λx μ-a.e., and invariant support tangent to this plane. At every nonzero x, tangency forces fixed z=(1+λ²)/(5−10λ²), then z-dot=0 fixes x² and each trajectory is an equilibrium; points with x=0 and z≠0 cannot support a compact invariant measure since z grows exponentially. Exact substitution of z±=(5±sqrt257)/100, λ±=(±sqrt257−15)/8 and r±=sqrt(7z±/(200λ±)) verifies the four equilibria. Endpoint equality measures are mixtures of 0 and the corresponding sign pair with nonzero mass, so any non-equilibrium ergodic state is strictly interior. Claim does not establish existence of strange-attractor measures.
